newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan court delays verdict of 27 Moslem students.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan court delays verdict of 27 Moslem students.

text.p: A Moroccan court on Friday postponed to next week issuing a verdict in a case involving 27 Moslem fundamentalist students accused of disturbing public order, the official MAP news agency reported.
A Casablanca-based lawyer said the students faced up to five years in jail. Two members of the group were not present during the court hearings, he said.
There was no explanation for the delay of the verdict. Court officials were not immediately available for comment.
The students appeared on Thursday and Friday before the Casablanca court on charges of "disturbing public order and violence against civil servants", the agency said.
The students were arrested two weeks ago after protests on a university campus to press demands for the improvement of their material conditions, including transportation, a union spokesman said.
Police say the students belong to the outlawed Islamic movement Al-Adl-Wal Ihsane (Justice and Charity) which is led by Sheikh Abdsalam Yassine who is spending his seventh year under house arrest.

The group was founded as a charity association in 1980. It applied for official recognition as a political party a year later but the interior ministry rejected the demand. The association was banned in 1990.

The court earlier this week sentenced three other students on similar charges. Oussama al-Hayouni received a two-year term in jail and his two colleagues Abdelfatah Kharbouch and Hassan Boukaffa, one year each, a lawyer said.
The government has announced that it was tightening control on student activities in universities in what officials said was a move to put an end to activities of the fundamentalists.
